tells.name: Placeholder people
tells.why_it_matters: Fake people and fake avatars. On a real site this is the single most damaging tell.
tells.fix: Real testimonials with permission, or none. Never invent people.

tells.name: Fake-looking proof
tells.why_it_matters: Round unverifiable numbers read as invented and destroy trust.
tells.fix: Use a real number you can back up, or drop the claim.

tells.name: The SaaS section skeleton
tells.why_it_matters: features + pricing + testimonials + faq, always in the same order. Structure is where AI output converges hardest.
tells.fix: Cut every section that doesn't serve YOUR product. Reorder around what your visitor actually asks first.

tells.name: Buzzword copy
tells.why_it_matters: Words like these fit 500 other products, which is exactly the problem - and they are the words AI reaches for first.
tells.fix: Replace each with the specific thing your product does ('saves you re-typing invoices' beats 'streamlines workflows').

tells.name: Round fake stats
tells.why_it_matters: Round unverifiable numbers ('10K+ users', '99.9% uptime'). On a new product they read as invented.
tells.fix: Real number or no number. 'Show more, claim less.'

tells.name: AI writing cadence
tells.why_it_matters: Two or more classic AI phrasings together ('it's not just X...', 'in today's fast-paced world').
tells.fix: Read it aloud. Rewrite in the words you'd say to a customer.

craft_flags.name: Tiny body text
craft_flags.why_it_matters: Lots of very small text. Body copy should be at least 16px (BDA guide).
craft_flags.fix: Reserve text-xs for true fine print; body at text-base (16px) or larger.

craft_flags.name: Uppercase running text
craft_flags.why_it_matters: Uppercase removes the word shapes dyslexic readers rely on (BDA guide). Fine for tiny labels, not for sentences.
craft_flags.fix: Use sentence case for anything longer than a word or two.
